title: Replacing hardcoded ethernet frame length with macro
description: Replacing hardcoded Ethernet frame length with macro in various files.

notes.body:
added 194 commits
  • 1c152629...a51d13f7 - 193 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • d540540f - Replacing hardcoded ethernet frame lenght with macro.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20957/diffs?diff_id=1463105336&start_sha=1c15262975c4b9eefbd5f4aae9e2dffa7e6e58bd)

The number 1514 is a somewhat arbitrary choice; it's probably a reasonable choice, given that most packets in network captures are *probably* either packets with Ethernet headers or packets whose lengths are limited by ensuring that the packets can be routed or bridged to Ethernet, but perhaps it should just be called `WTAP_DEFAULT_FRAME_LEN`. (We may well pick a larger value, e.g. a power-of-2 value, at some point.)

Are you saying that this shouldn't be a blind search/replace of 1514 -> WTAP_DEFAULT_ETH_FRAME_LEN and that some of the 1514 values changed in the MR aren't directly related to WTAP?  Because not all WTAP frames are ethernet, so I liked including it in the prefix.

> Are you saying that this shouldn't be a blind search/replace of 1514 -\> WTAP_DEFAULT_ETH_FRAME_LEN

Yes.

> and that some of the 1514 values changed in the MR aren't directly related to WTAP?

No, that they aren't directly related to ETH.

The current value being used is `SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE`, which works better.

In some cases, we might already know the maximum size, and should perhaps use that, but this is a good start.

Perhaps we should define `DEFAULT_INIT_BUFFER_SIZE` to `SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE` and use that.
